## Why

Coursera hands you notebooks. Real analysis work is usually scripts. You need both to feel ordinary in Positron, and you need the formatter and the package list to work without you thinking about them.

This is also the check most likely to send you back to VS Code, so log every pull you feel.

## What you will have at the end

- Your lab notebook worked in Positron's notebook editor
- A Python script and an R script, each run cell by cell
- Format-on-save working for both languages in this folder
- A quick way to see which packages a session has

**Time box:** 45 minutes on top of your lab. The R half is capped at 20.

## How to work this file

- Each task states an outcome. Finding the how is part of the check.
- Where a task asks you to predict, write the prediction before you test it.
- The hint names the Positron docs page to read if you get stuck. Use it only after trying.

## Python half

### 1. Work the lab in the notebook editor

Do your lab in Positron's notebook editor. Arrange the window so the notebook, your variables, and your plots are visible together.

### 2. Know what gets saved

**Predict first:** when you save the notebook, does the `.ipynb` file keep cell outputs? Does it keep execution counts?

**Answer:**

Check the settings that control this.

## R half (20-minute cap)

### 7. A script in sections

Create `scratch.R` with three short sections on your lab's dataset: load, summarise, plot. Mark the sections the way you would in RStudio. Run it section by section.

*Hint: "Code Cells".*

**Predict first:** will your RStudio-style section headers work as cell boundaries here?

**Answer:**

**After testing, were you right?**

**Answer:**

**Is the keystroke for running one line or statement the same as in RStudio?**

### 8. Set up Air

Positron ships with Air, an R formatter. Initialise it for this folder and get format-on-save working for R.

*Hint: "Formatting R code with Air".*

## Checks

- [ ] I completed a Coursera lab in Positron's notebook editor
- [ ] I know what Positron saves into an `.ipynb` file
- [ ] I can run a Python script and an R script cell by cell
- [ ] Format-on-save works for Python and for R in this folder
- [ ] I can check a package version without typing a command
- [ ] I did the R half in 20 minutes or less
